options.content:
Hypervisor: **${gvar_oie_hypervisor:text}** · Project: **${gvar_oie_project_uuid:text}** · Name filter: **${gvar_oie_project_name:text}** · Instance: **${gvar_oie_instance_uuid:text}**

**VM view from the hypervisor:** Libvirt/QEMU and host networking show VM resource use and activity. Ceph/RBD, physical disks, NICs and switches observe other points in the path and can report different values.

Graphs group VMs by project; partial collection can understate totals. A carried instance filter narrows snapshots, inventory, storage overview and retypes. **Open this panel’s info help for ranking, legends and missing-data guidance.**

panels.description:
Graphs follow the selected time range; snapshot counts and tables use its end unless the panel says selected range. Project graphs group instances by project. The carried instance filter only narrows snapshots, inventory, storage overview and retypes; Reset scope clears it.

Ranking: Top projects and Top instances limit ranked graphs, not tables. Comparison panels share a selected set; their help names the ranking measurement. List, direction and source companions can produce more than N lines. 0 (All) uses the large graph limit. Selection stays fixed over the range. Max in range uses the highest plotted ranking value, Mean its average, and Last observed its latest available sample, which can predate the range end. Ranking uses the graph sampling interval and can miss a raw scrape between plotted points.

Legends: Max is the highest plotted sample, not an individual I/O maximum; Last is the right-edge value and is unavailable for an ended series. Click a value heading to sort or a series name to isolate it; scroll for remaining rows. Legend sorting does not select different projects or instances. Names are metadata; full UUIDs distinguish duplicate names.

Display: resource and activity line colours identify entities or measurements, not health, and can repeat. Coverage and retype panels explain their status colours separately. Line styles distinguish paired measurements. Fill intensity follows the plot’s magnitude and can change with zoom or filters; it is not a severity score. Percentages use the denominator named by the panel. High use alone does not establish a fault. Byte and bit axes use binary prefixes.

Gaps and Unavailable mean the required observation is missing, idle or outside its usable window, as explained in the panel. They are not invented zeroes. Available-source project activity can understate totals during partial coverage; check the collection panels. Tables return all matching rows: scroll and sort columns, and use Inspect → Data for retained identifiers.

panels.title: CPU and memory · use relative to VM allocation

panels.description:
Project CPU use as a percentage of allocated vCPUs, weighted by each instance’s vCPU count. CPU measurements use a one-minute mean. This describes use of the configured allocation, not performance quality or physical host occupancy.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU CPU counters collected on the hypervisor by OIE. This host-side view can differ from guest reporting; reboot, migration and short windows can make it spiky.

Every matching observed active instance must have both a vCPU count and CPU measurement on a usable Libvirt source. Missing instances or dimensions produce a gap rather than zero use. Top projects ranks this percentage; general ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.

panels.title: CPU use / allocated vCPUs (%)

panels.description:
Project guest-view used-memory estimate divided by configured instance memory allocation, as a percentage. A low value can indicate unused guest capacity; it does not prove that physical host RAM can be reclaimed.

Source: Libvirt balloon current minus balloon usable; usable corresponds to guest MemAvailable. This is not QEMU RSS, unique physical host consumption or QEMU overhead.

panels.title: Observed memory allocation · by project

panels.description:
Aggregate host-scheduler runqueue delay across VM vCPUs in each project, in milliseconds of waiting per wall-clock second (ms/s). Libvirt delay/steal is preferred per vCPU and wait is used only as a compatibility fallback; the two aliases are never added.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU vCPU delay and wait counters collected by OIE.
Limitations: Counters can reset on VM reboot or migration; short rate windows can be spiky.

Display: milliseconds of scheduler waiting per wall-clock second, summed across vCPUs. For example, 100 ms/s means the project’s vCPUs accumulated 100 milliseconds of waiting per elapsed second. This is a rate of accumulated waiting, not per-request latency or a CPU percentage; multiple vCPUs can total more than 1000 ms/s.

Top projects limits this graph to the selected projects with the highest values; it does not limit tables. Ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.

Unusable collection sources produce gaps. Short rolling-window counters can remain visible after a VM stops while their source is usable.

Values use available selected-source observations. Partial collection coverage can understate project totals; see the collection coverage panels.

An instance’s scheduler value requires its complete configured vCPU cohort. A missing vCPU counter is not zero waiting; an incomplete cohort is unavailable.

panels.description:
Scope: this describes availability of the OIE/Libvirt observations used by the VM disk-latency panels; it is not storage-backend health coverage.

Healthy targets have a successful scrape and recent successful Libvirt collection. Selected targets counts the OIE scrape targets still known to Prometheus, including failed targets. These counts follow the hypervisor selector; project and VM selectors cannot establish ownership on an unavailable host. Removed scrape targets are outside this denominator. A healthy target does not guarantee every disk has timing counters.

Scope: running VMs with qualifying current Libvirt/QEMU observations at each evaluation time. This is an operation-weighted mean of VM virtual-block timing counters, not direct Ceph/storage-backend latency, physical-media latency, or application fsync latency. A high value can justify backend investigation but does not identify which layer caused it. In the legend, Max is the highest plotted mean in the selected range, not the slowest individual I/O.

Five-minute I/O-weighted mean: total observed operation time / total observed operations, in milliseconds. Each direction uses matching current time/request counters with equal sample counts, from running VMs on healthy, fresh Libvirt targets. Idle or unmeasured groups produce gaps. This is the measured subset, not a percentile or a physical-drive measurement. Use the coverage counts below to see missing measurements. Storage source is the discovered disk_type label: an RBD pool name or a source kind such as local. It does not identify HDD, SSD or NVMe; local means file-backed and can reside on shared storage. All matching sources are shown; Top N controls do not trim this section.

No measured read I/O can mean no completed read operations in the window or missing/invalid timing observations. It is not zero latency. Check the matching measurement-coverage table and source health.

panels.title: VM disk flush latency by source · 5m mean
VM disk latency and observation coverage
panels.description:
At the selected range end, one row per project UUID and storage source for VM virtual-block observations. Latency is a five-minute I/O-weighted mean: total observed operation time divided by total observed operations, in milliseconds. It covers running VMs with usable, fresh Libvirt/QEMU observations and matching current time/request counters with equal sample counts. It is not direct Ceph/storage-backend latency, physical-media latency, application fsync latency or a percentile. A high mean does not identify the layer that caused it.

Coverage: Observed devices counts runtime block-device observations on VMs last observed running, including retained observations on unhealthy targets. It is not a physical-disk count and is not limited to configured device=disk attachments. Read/Write/Flush measured counts attachments with usable paired counters, including idle devices. Compare measured counts with observed devices, and healthy with selected targets; missing inventory can still hide disks. Read + write IOPS requires both request counters, but does not require timing counters.

Idle directions with usable counters show No read/write/flush I/O in 5m; directions without usable timing evidence show Unavailable. Both retain their columns. Idle latency is undefined, not 0 ms. Measured-count columns show counter availability, not completed operations.

Storage source is the discovered disk_type label: an RBD pool name or source kind such as local. It does not identify HDD, SSD, NVMe or a guaranteed Cinder volume type; local means file-backed and can reside on shared storage. Unclassified source means the runtime device could not be matched to a recognised source. Known config drives, CD-ROMs and floppies belong to configured inventory, not disk-performance metrics. Unmatched runtime targets remain unclassified until XML and runtime identity agree. Open Selected instances · disk source observations on the Instance dashboard to identify the VM, device and inventory match.

All matching rows are returned; Top N does not trim this table. Narrow the dashboard scope, scroll within the table, or click column headings to sort. Project links retain UUID identity even with duplicate names. Inspect → Data with field overrides disabled exposes retained identifiers and additional columns.

panels.title: Storage · VM project activity and attached logical capacity

panels.description:
Scope: VM virtual-disk counters observed through Libvirt/QEMU. These represent VM-side block activity seen at the hypervisor, not total backend operations, backend device utilization, or storage-pool performance. Caching, request merging, replication, snapshots, and other storage layers can make backend I/O differ.

Aggregated disk read throughput per project (bytes/s with automatic IEC prefixes) across all instances.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.

Top projects limits this graph to the selected projects with the highest values; it does not limit tables. Ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.

Unusable collection sources produce gaps. Short rolling-window counters can remain visible after a VM stops while their source is usable.

Values use available selected-source observations. Partial collection coverage can understate project totals; see the collection coverage panels.

panels.title: VM disk write IOPS · by project

panels.description:
Scope: running VMs with qualifying current Libvirt/QEMU observations at each evaluation time. This is an operation-weighted mean of VM virtual-block timing counters, not direct Ceph/storage-backend latency, physical-media latency, or application fsync latency. A high value can justify backend investigation but does not identify which layer caused it. In the legend, Max is the highest plotted mean in the selected range, not the slowest individual I/O.

IO-weighted average disk latency across the project.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.

I/O-weighted calculation: summed service time divided by summed operations. Both sums use the same disks, operation direction, rate window and sample counts; unsupported or currently missing counter pairs are omitted together. This is latency for the observed disk cohort. It excludes unmeasured disks and is not an average of per-disk averages. No operations or unavailable Libvirt telemetry produces a gap; zero latency is not invented.

Ranking controls: Top projects selects up to N projects using the highest available read or write latency. Available companion measurements use those same selected projects; they do not independently select their own top projects. Companion measurements can produce more than N lines in the panel. Ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.

panels.title: VM disk latency · by project (1m I/O-weighted mean)

panels.description:
Scope: VM virtual-disk counters observed through Libvirt/QEMU. These represent VM-side block activity seen at the hypervisor, not total backend operations, backend device utilization, or storage-pool performance. Caching, request merging, replication, snapshots, and other storage layers can make backend I/O differ.

Flush and write operations per second, summed by project. Frequent flushes can indicate a workload requesting durability, but do not measure application fsync latency or backend durability.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.

Ranking controls: Top projects selects up to N projects using combined available flush and write IOPS. Available companion measurements use those same selected projects; they do not independently select their own top projects. Companion measurements can produce more than N lines in the panel. Ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.

Unusable collection sources produce gaps. Short rolling-window counters can remain visible after a VM stops while their source is usable.

Values use available selected-source observations. Partial collection coverage can understate project totals; see the collection coverage panels.

panels.description:
Scope: guest-visible logical disk/attachment capacity reported for VMs. This is not Ceph/storage-pool capacity, physical bytes consumed, backend free space, or a measure of available storage performance.

Reported guest-visible logical disk sizes, grouped by the existing disk_type label. That label contains a source type or pool name; it does not reliably identify the storage backend. In particular, local means a file source in the existing exporter label and does not prove local physical storage. A pool name alone does not prove RBD.

This is provisioned address space for observed disk attachments, not used bytes, free space, guest-filesystem usage, or physical backend consumption. A shared disk can be counted once per observed attachment. Missing capacity observations are omitted; absent or unreachable hosts are not a complete inventory. The existing paired capacity/offset view is available in the collapsed Disk address-space diagnostics row.

Top projects ranks total reported logical capacity; source/pool lines for the selected projects are then shown. A project can have several source lines. Ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.

panels.title: Disk address-space diagnostic (not space usage)
Storage · attached-volume retypes
Attached-volume retype overview
panels.description:
OIE observes attached Cinder RBD retypes from the VM-facing Libvirt/QEMU block-job path on the hypervisor. Each operation is identified by instance, disk, source RBD image/pool and destination RBD image/pool, so concurrent retypes on one hypervisor remain separate. Cinder remains authoritative for the control-plane operation and its lifecycle timestamps.

Status codes: 1 = copying/finalizing, 2 = terminal observation with the destination as the live source, 3 = terminal observation with the original source still live (unsuccessful/cancelled), 4 = terminal observation with an unmatched final source, 5 = copy ready/awaiting pivot, 6 = ready/awaiting pivot for at least ten minutes.

“Now” fields use current OIE observations; outcome fields count operation identities with that terminal status anywhere in the selected Grafana time range. Monitoring coverage is the fraction of currently reporting selected exporters with retype monitoring enabled; target availability above remains authoritative for unreachable exporters. Current-stage counts fall back to zero only when all selected Libvirt sources are usable and at least one exporter has monitoring enabled. Positive bounded observations remain visible during their source-defined grace window. Captured outcome counts retain their selected-range history.

Zero counts are neutral. Coloured values identify active stages or observed outcomes; the panel background stays neutral.

panels.description:
OIE observes attached Cinder RBD retypes from the VM-facing Libvirt/QEMU block-job path on the hypervisor. Each operation is identified by instance, disk, source RBD image/pool and destination RBD image/pool, so concurrent retypes on one hypervisor remain separate. Cinder remains authoritative for the control-plane operation and its lifecycle timestamps.

Status codes: 1 = copying/finalizing, 2 = terminal observation with the destination as the live source, 3 = terminal observation with the original source still live (unsuccessful/cancelled), 4 = terminal observation with an unmatched final source, 5 = copy ready/awaiting pivot, 6 = ready/awaiting pivot for at least ten minutes.

This table contains only operations whose Libvirt block job was confirmed present within OIE’s bounded active-observation window. Logical Progress is the current estimated work position; Observed Elapsed is time since OIE first saw the operation. Source/Destination RBD Image identify the exact backing images so multiple retypes on one hypervisor or instance remain separate. Missing optional measurements remain unavailable; their table columns stay visible.

panels.description:
Scope: VM virtual-interface counters observed through Libvirt/QEMU. These are not physical NIC, switch, or fabric telemetry; encapsulation, offload, host traffic, and network-path behavior can differ from the VM counters.

Aggregated inbound network throughput per project (bits/s with automatic IEC prefixes, across all instances).

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky.

Top projects limits this graph to the selected projects with the highest values; it does not limit tables. Ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.

Unusable collection sources produce gaps. Short rolling-window counters can remain visible after a VM stops while their source is usable.

Values use available selected-source observations. Partial collection coverage can understate project totals; see the collection coverage panels.

panels.title: VM-attributed inbound conntrack flows · by project

panels.description:
VM endpoint matches in each project as a percentage of the selected hosts’ configured conntrack entry limit. Use this to compare attributed connection load with the available host-table limits.

This is endpoint attribution, not host-table utilization. One connection between two VMs can count at both endpoints, so these percentages can exceed 100% and must not be added as project capacity shares. For actual table utilization, use the Hypervisor conntrack utilization panel.

Both counts are summed across the selected hosts with usable collection; project filters narrow the endpoint count. Missing or stale observations leave gaps. See collection coverage before comparing projects. NAT, asymmetric routing and incomplete or ambiguous fixed-IP mapping can limit attribution.

Source: Linux kernel conntrack state attributed to observed VM fixed IPs. Host limits are the configured kernel table limits. Top projects ranks this panel’s ratio; graph selection is fixed over the selected range. See the scope panel and ranking controls for shared viewing guidance.
panels.title: VM endpoint matches / host entry limit (%)

panels.description:
Average number of VM endpoint matches in each project per observed kernel conntrack entry. A value of 1.86× means 186 endpoint matches for every 100 host entries; it does not mean that a host table is 186% full.

One connection between two VMs can contribute one match at its source VM and one at its destination VM. If both VMs belong to the same project, both matches contribute to that project. Endpoint matches and host entries are summed across the selected usable hosts, so multiple hosts alone do not make the ratio exceed 1×. This measures endpoint attribution, not a distinct project share or host-table utilization.

Project filters narrow the endpoint matches; the denominator includes host entries from all selected usable hosts. Missing or stale observations leave gaps. NAT, asymmetric routing and incomplete or ambiguous fixed-IP mapping can limit attribution; check collection coverage before comparing projects.

Source: Linux kernel conntrack state attributed to observed VM fixed IPs. Top projects ranks this panel’s endpoint-match ratio; graph selection is fixed over the selected range. See the scope panel and ranking controls for shared viewing guidance.

panels.title: Threat-list flow matches · by project and direction

panels.description:
Threat-list contact events observed during each Prometheus $__rate_interval. Each point is an interval delta from increase(...), not a per-second rate.

Source: Linux kernel conntrack state evaluated against the configured threat lists on each hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: These are bounded observations of host-visible conntrack activity. Counter resets are handled by Prometheus increase(), while scrape gaps can reduce confidence.

Ranking controls: Top projects selects up to N projects using available threat-list contact totals per project, all lists and directions combined. Available companion measurements use those same selected projects; they do not independently select their own top projects. Companion measurements can produce more than N lines in the panel. Ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.

Unusable collection sources produce gaps. Short rolling-window counters can remain visible after a VM stops while their source is usable.

Values use available selected-source observations. Partial collection coverage can understate project totals; see the collection coverage panels.

Inventory · grouped configuration
panels.description: Configured VM definitions and block-device presence. Configuration is not runtime activity or evidence of guest use.

Last observed count of active Libvirt domains per project on the selected hypervisors, from OIE’s retained runtime instance configuration. This includes paused active domains and excludes inactive definitions; it is not the Running instances count. Source: hypervisor-derived instance/project mapping.

Source failures can preserve this count and rebuilds or migrations can temporarily affect mapping. It is not a current complete Nova inventory or a traffic-based count. Use the inventory summary and collection coverage to assess current observations. Top projects ranks this count; ranking and legend help is in the scope panel.
panels.title: Last observed active VM count · by project
Inventory summary · selected scope
panels.description: Inventory counts for the selected project and instance scope at the range end. Observed instances includes every instance definition currently seen through Libvirt, whether running, paused or inactive. Running instances is therefore a subset of observed instances; when every observed instance is running, the two counts are equal. A migrating instance can be observed on more than one hypervisor. All selected exporter sources must be usable for a complete count. A healthy empty selection reports zero; any selected missing or unhealthy source reports Unavailable.

panels.description:
Observed instances means all instance definitions currently seen through Libvirt in this scope, including both running and inactive instances. The Running, Shutoff and Other states columns break that observed total down by current Libvirt state. A migrating instance can be observed on more than one hypervisor, so these are OIE hypervisor observations rather than an authoritative Nova inventory.

All matching rows are returned; Top N affects graphs only. Scroll within the table and click column headings to sort. Full UUIDs remain in Inspect → Data and links.

Only usable target observations contribute rows. Failed targets can hide instances; target and source coverage above identify missing observation coverage.

panels.title: Exporter and collection · coverage

panels.description:
Counts of selected exporter targets over time. Usable requires a successful scrape, successful source collection and a nonnegative source age within max(3 collection intervals, 60 seconds). Unusable includes failed scrapes, failed collection, never-successful and stale sources. Unknown means the target exists but required source metadata is missing. Each target belongs to one category per source. Missing target inventory leaves a gap. Source coverage applies to every project on a host.

Legend values are host counts, not a status assigned to the entire cluster. Missing status = 0 means no selected hosts have missing collection metadata.

Colour identifies state: mint usable, red unusable, grey missing. Libvirt is solid; conntrack is dashed.

list.label: Project

list.description: Project name and full UUID. Filtering and links use the UUID, so duplicate names remain distinct.

list.label: Project name filter
list.name: gvar_oie_project_name
list.description: Additional name filter applied to the selected project UUIDs. Leave All to include every selected project, including duplicate names.

list.label: Instance (name | UUID)
list.name: gvar_oie_instance_uuid
list.description: Names are for display; every selection and link filters by the instance UUID.

list.name: gvar_oie_top_projects
list.label: Top projects / query
list.description: Maximum ranked projects in graphs. Comparison panels use a shared project set; panel help names the ranking measurement. Source, direction and list companions can produce more than N lines. 0 (All) uses the large graph limit. Tables remain unlimited.

list.name: gvar_oie_rank_projects_by
list.label: Select projects by
list.query: Last observed : last_over_time,Max in range : max_over_time,Mean in range : avg_over_time
list.description: Rank projects by the highest plotted value (Max), average plotted value (Mean), or latest available sample (Last observed). Last observed can include ended series. Comparison panels use the ranking measurement named in their help. Legend sorting changes display order only.

list.name: gvar_oie_top_instances
list.label: Top instances / query
list.description: Maximum matching series per graph query, not a guaranteed number of lines or visible legend rows. Multiple queries can each return N series. 0 (All) uses the existing large graph limit. Tables are not limited.

list.name: gvar_oie_rank_instances_by
list.label: Select instances by
list.query: Last observed : last_over_time,Max in range : max_over_time,Mean in range : avg_over_time
list.description: Rank instances by the highest plotted value (Max), average plotted value (Mean), or latest available sample (Last observed). Last observed can predate the range end. Saved URL selections remain active; legend sorting changes display order only.
